name: Parque das Nações
seoTitle: Parque das Nações by Train from the Cruise Terminal
tagline: Flat riverside district built for Expo '98, easiest by train to Oriente, best for families and anyone who wants Lisbon without hills

description.short: The former Expo '98 site on Lisbon's eastern riverfront, now a residential and business district with a long flat promenade. It holds the Oceanário, the Pavilhão do Conhecimento science centre and the riverside cable car, about 7.4 km from the cruise terminal.
description.full:
Parque das Nações is the opposite of the Lisbon most cruise passengers come for: no hills, no cobbles and almost nothing older than 1998. It makes sense on a port day if you are travelling with children or someone who struggles on slopes, if it is raining and you want the Oceanário, or if you have been to Lisbon before and want to see a different side of it.

From the ship, walk about 10 minutes to Santa Apolónia and take a suburban train to Oriente; the ride is around seven minutes and trains run several times an hour. A taxi from the terminal takes about 15 minutes. Oriente station, designed by Santiago Calatrava, is the gateway: walk through the Vasco da Gama shopping centre to reach the river.

With two hours, see the station roof, walk down to the waterfront and along to the Oceanário, then take the cable car north over the river's edge and walk back towards Oriente. With half a day, add the Oceanário itself (allow 90 minutes to two hours) or the Pavilhão do Conhecimento, a hands-on science centre that suits children of primary-school age. From 7 September 2026 the Pavilhão is closed on Mondays.

The public spaces are free. The Oceanário charges adults €25.50 to €29.90 depending on the entry slot, the Pavilhão €15 and the cable car €7.50 one way or €9.50 return. Weekends and school holidays are the busiest times at the attractions; on weekdays the promenade is quiet. There is little shade along the river, so bring water and sun protection in summer.

Skip the shopping centre unless you need something specific, and do not expect to fit Parque das Nações and Belém into one short call: they sit at opposite ends of the city.
description.history: Until the 1990s this stretch of the eastern riverfront was an industrial zone of oil depots, warehouses and port installations. It was cleared and rebuilt for Expo '98, the world's fair held from 22 May to 30 September 1998 to mark 500 years since Vasco da Gama reached India, under the theme 'The Oceans, a Heritage for the Future'. Several of today's landmarks were Expo buildings: the Oceans Pavilion became the Oceanário, Álvaro Siza's Portugal Pavilion kept its suspended concrete canopy, and the cable car and Oriente station opened that year. After the fair the site was turned into a permanent district of housing, offices and parks.
description.significance: It is Lisbon's largest example of urban regeneration and the only part of the city laid out on the flat, with wide promenades and step-free routes. For cruise passengers that matters more than the architecture: it is the most accessible area in Lisbon for wheelchairs and pushchairs, and it groups the Oceanário, a science centre and the cable car within a 15-minute walk of each other.

directions.general: Located along Lisbon's eastern waterfront on the Tejo River, extending from Oriente station to the Vasco da Gama Bridge
directions.fromCruisePort: About 7.4 km north-east. Take the train from Santa Apolónia station (10 minutes' walk from the terminal) to Oriente, which is the entrance to the district. Taxi about 15 minutes.
directions.publicTransport: Metro: Red Line to Oriente station (main hub). Buses: 705, 708, 725, 728, 744, 750, 759, 782, 794. Train: Oriente station connects to regional and national services.
directions.parking: Multiple paid parking facilities including Centro Vasco da Gama, Oceanário, and street parking

openingTimes.currentStatus: Public spaces open at all times; attractions keep their own hours

seasonal.hours: Public promenade and gardens open 24 hours
seasonal.notes: Oceanário 10:00-20:00 daily; Pavilhão do Conhecimento Tue-Fri 10:00-18:00, weekends and holidays 10:00-19:00 (closed Mondays from 7 September 2026); cable car 11:00-19:00 until 23 October 2026, then 11:00-18:00

admissionPrices.notes: The district itself is free. Attraction prices for adults: Oceanário €25.50-€29.90 depending on entry time; Pavilhão do Conhecimento €15 (youth 3-17 €10, seniors €11); cable car €7.50 one way, €9.50 return.

visitingInformation.averageVisitDuration: 2 hours for the promenade and cable car; half a day with the Oceanário
visitingInformation.bestTimeToVisit: Weekday mornings for the attractions; late afternoon for the river light. Avoid weekends and school holidays at the Oceanário if you can.
busyPeriods: Concert and trade-fair days at the arena and FIL
visitingInformation.adviceForVisitors: Arrive by suburban train from Santa Apolónia to Oriente. Walk through the shopping centre to the river. Bring water and sun protection in summer, as the promenade has little shade.

cruisePassengerInfo.timeNeededFromPort: About 2.5-3 hours return for the promenade and cable car; 4-4.5 hours if you add the Oceanário
cruisePassengerInfo.accessibility: Train from Santa Apolónia (10 minutes' walk from the ship) to Oriente, or a 15-minute taxi. Once there, the district is flat and step-free.
tips: Take a suburban train from Santa Apolónia to Oriente (about 7 minutes, several an hour); long-distance Alfa Pendular and Intercidades trains need a separate reserved ticket.
From Oriente station, walk through the Vasco da Gama shopping centre to reach the riverfront.
The Oceanário is cheapest from 16:00 (€25.50 adults) and dearest between 10:00 and 11:30 (€29.90).
The Pavilhão do Conhecimento science centre is closed on Mondays from 7 September 2026.
Ride the cable car one way (€7.50) and walk back along the river rather than paying €9.50 for a return.
There is little shade on the promenade; bring water and a hat between May and September.
Parque das Nações and Belém are at opposite ends of Lisbon; on a short call, pick one.
For a group of three or four, or anyone with limited mobility, a taxi from the terminal (about 15 minutes) saves the walk to Santa Apolónia and through the shopping centre.

highlights: Oriente station, designed by Santiago Calatrava for Expo '98
Oceanário de Lisboa on the Doca dos Olivais
Pavilhão do Conhecimento, a hands-on science centre
Telecabine Lisboa, the riverside cable car (1,230 m)
Álvaro Siza's Portugal Pavilion with its suspended concrete canopy
Riverside promenade with views of the Vasco da Gama Bridge
Jardins Garcia de Orta and the Jardins da Água, free public gardens
facilities: Oriente station: suburban and long-distance trains, metro Red Line and buses
Vasco da Gama shopping centre beside the station, with a food court
Restaurants and cafés along the waterfront
Toilets inside the main attractions and the shopping centre
ATMs in the shopping centre and station

accessibility.mobilityNotes: Flat, wide promenades with step-free routes between the main attractions. Lifts at Oriente station and in the shopping centre. Distances add up, so allow for 15-20 minutes on foot between the station and the Oceanário.
